chapters.summary: Caitlin Krause, founder of Rising Tide Effect and Water Safety Coalition member, says 113 New Yorkers drowned in 2024 and most deaths were preventable. She describes witnessing a drowning at Beach 17th Street and calls for an Office of Water Safety, school-based water safety education, transparent DOE pool permitting, year-round nonprofit pool access, and weekend-only lifeguard positions.
chapters.title: Caitlin Krause urges Office of Water Safety and school water safety education

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Hankerson and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: My name is Caitlin Krause.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: I'm the founder and executive director of Rising Tide Effect and a member of the Water Safety Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: In 2024, there were 113 New Yorkers that died by drowning, and most of those deaths were preventable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: I've seen what this looks like up close.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: In July of 2025, I was at...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Beach 17th Street in the moments after someone went under.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: They drowned because they didn't know what the current about the current there and the sudden drop offs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: They had no way of knowing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: And that's what happens when hazards go unmarked and people never learn to read the water.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: So firstly, I think that New York City needs an office of water safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: It's currently spread across six agencies with no one accountable for the whole picture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Without coordination, the bills before you today can't reach their full potential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Second, water safety education belongs in our schools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: It's not all on parks to deliver water safety education for the entire city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Every child should leave school knowing how to recognize risk and stay safe around the water, and this can be accomplished in the classroom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: We urge the council to build on its 2017 resolution, support classroom-based water safety education, and lead New York State in a Water Safety Education in Schools Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Third, communities need access to swim lessons, and that starts with pools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: DOE pool permitting should be transparent so nonprofits know which pools are available and how to apply.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: City-owned pools, including parks pools, should be open to nonprofits year-round.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Organizations like ours are ready to fill the gaps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: And fourth, a longer beach season needs more lifeguards, and that pipeline starts with swimmers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: core pathway, rising tide effect, youth trained to become New York City Parks lifeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: The city should invest in programs like this and bring back weekend-only lifeguard positions, as was the case until about 30 years ago, which will immediately expand experienced lifeguards in the empty chairs on our beaches.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: As summers grow hotter, more New Yorkers will head to the water.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Whether or not there's a lifeguard on duty, and whether or not they know how to swim.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Caitlin Krause
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Olga Perez, founder of MVP Lifeguards and MVP Swimmers, describes teaching children to swim and certifying lifeguards. She asks the Council to expand the Connect Kids to Parks grant for swim lessons, establish year-round water safety funding, expand public and school pool access, invest in youth lifeguard pathways, advance a high school PE credit resolution, and expedite Bronx pool renovations.
chapters.title: Olga Perez asks Council to expand swim lessons and Bronx pool renovations

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: I couldn't agree more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairperson and distinguished members of the City Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: My name is Olga Perez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: I'm the founder of MVP Lifeguards and the Executive Director of MVP Swimmers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: For over 25 years, my life purpose has been teaching children to swim and training teenagers to become certified lifeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Through our partnership with the CDC Foundation, MVP Swimmers has provided swimming and water safety education to approximately 400 elementary school children in grades 2 through 5.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Through our Department of Youth and Community Development Making Waves program, MVP Lifeguards has taught over 1,000 children to swim and certified over 20 lifeguards annually since 2022.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Last week, I participated in a SOMOS conference panel in Puerto Rico titled Del Barrio a la Piscina, alongside Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan and Yonkers Mayor Mike Soprano.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: discussing drowning prevention, expanding swimming programs, and lifeguard recruitments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: These conversations reinforce that access to swimming education is a statewide public safety concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: I commend Governor Hochul and the New York State for investing nearly $260 million in swimming facilities through New York Swims and allocating $5 million for free swimming lessons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: These investments represent meaningful progress, particularly for underserved communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: However, I noticed a gap in the Connect Kids to Parks Field Trip Grant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: It reimburses $2,500 per eligible field trips, but excludes swimming instruction fees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Getting a child to the pool is not the same as teaching that child how to survive in the water.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Today, I respectfully ask this council to support six actions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: First, advocate that New York State to expand the Connect Kids to Park field trip grant to fund progressive multi-session swimming lessons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Second, to establish sustainable year-round funding for water safety education with opportunities for qualified community-based providers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Third, to expand access to public and school pools for qualified community organizations like MVP Swimmers and many others.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Fourth,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: to invest in youth lifeguard training and employment pathways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: And fifth, to advance Resolution 251-2024, recognizing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: lifeguard training towards a high school physical education credit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: And six, and this one hits home because I'm a resident of the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: We need to prioritize and expedite outstanding swimming pool renovations in the Bronx, including Evander Charles Educational Campus, Theodore Roosevelt Educational Campus,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: PSMS 4, PSMS 363 with clear timelines and reopening because we're talking about water safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: And in order to give our kids access, our pools need to be renovated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Can you repeat those locations for me?

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Evander Charles Educational Campus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Theodore Roosevelt Educational Campus, PSMS 4, and PSMS 363.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: 363 was the last one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Alec Webley, co-president of Team New York Aquatics, says the city's lifeguard program is designed in a way that excludes working professionals, including hundreds of proficient swimmers in his organization. He also asks Parks to allow community groups to permit city pools at low-use times to expand swim programs and lifeguard recruitment.
chapters.title: Alec Webley says lifeguard program excludes working professionals

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: How are you?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Chair Hankerson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: My name is Alec Webley, and I am one of the co-presidents of Team New York Aquatics.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: We are New York City's LGBTQ swimming, water polo, and artistic swimming team.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: With over 1,000 members and affiliates and offerings of those sports, as well as Adult Learn to Swim, we are the largest LGBTQ-inclusive aquatics charity in the United States, as well as being a proud member of the Water Safety Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: And we're particularly proud to have provided among the cheapest adult learn to swim programming, including 100% scholarships to nearly half of the 200 adults we taught to swim this year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: I want to speak to two issues briefly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: The first respects lifeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: I represent 500 very proficient swimmers who are going to international competitions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: Not one of us is able to be a New York City lifeguard because the lifeguard program has been specifically designed to not accommodate working professionals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: There is absolutely no need for the lifeguard program not to accommodate working professionals, and I know because I also hire a bunch of lifeguards who are working professionals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: It simply requires that the training and qualifications be structured in such a way that they are able to be accessed by people who are working in the field.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: 9 to 5.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: Parks repeatedly talks about how they can't expand the season because they have all of these college students, and that's a legitimate concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: But there are hundreds of gay men who can't afford Fire Island Pines chairs, given their scandalously high prices, who would be only too delighted to work on their tans on the city beaches.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: We want a lifeguard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: We would have no problem lifeguarding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: We would love to be part of this program, and it's simply the bureaucratic structure of lifeguarding that is preventing us from taking part.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: The second thing I would emphasize is that for many community groups, it is bureaucracy rather than anything else that's preventing us from efficiently utilizing pools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: And as just one example, the Parks Department allows permitting of sports fields, but does not allow permitting, including at low use times like early mornings and late evenings, of city pools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: Allow community groups to permit those pools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: We can run more programs, bring more adults into swimming, and then have a larger pool of recruits for lifeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alec Webley
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Before she left, Councilmember Linda Lee mentioned that she potentially wanted to be a lifeguard, but I was going to ask her.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: I don't know how that's possible given...

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Your work schedule.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: So thank you for highlighting that.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: You may be good.

chapters.summary: Shanna Blanchard, chair of the Water Safety Coalition, says the coalition supports the goals of the bills but the docket falls short. She calls for an Office of Water Safety, a follow-up hearing in January 2027, pairing any season extension with lifeguard corps reforms, and a school water safety education bill.
chapters.title: Shanna Blanchard presents Water Safety Coalition priorities

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Hankerson and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: My name is Shanna Blanchard and I chair the Water Safety Coalition, a network of New York City residents, community groups, and nonprofit organizations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: committed to making water safety an essential right for all, to save lives, and to create a more inclusive recreation community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: On behalf of our members, many of whom are here today, thank you for holding this hearing and for your commitment to water safety in our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: We are grateful to this committee and the council for bringing attention to an issue that touches so many New Yorkers, and we appreciate the work your offices have put into the bills before you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: I also want to congratulate the Parks Department on their successes this season and reaching some milestones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: The coalition supports the goals behind every bill on today's docket.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Longer and safer beach and pool seasons, clearer rip current warnings and educational signage, and more access to swimming and water safety programming.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Our concern is not with the intent of these bills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: It is that this docket on its own falls short of what the moment requires and that key legislation needed to make these bills work is missing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Simply put, it is not enough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: In 2027, we hope the council will make water safety a standing priority and move from discussion to substantive policy change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: According to the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, New York City saw 113 drowning deaths in 2024.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: With intensifying heat each summer, we expect that number to rise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: The communities hit hardest are the ones with the least access to pools, lifeguards, and swim instruction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Water safety needs to be a citywide priority with a comprehensive structure and plan to match.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: That structure is the missing piece, an office of water safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Water safety in our city is spread across many agencies and no single entity is responsible for coordinating them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: We had hoped the legislation to create the Office of Water Safety would be part of today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Without it, several of the bills before you cannot be effectively considered or implemented.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Take the interactive map of publicly owned pools, intro 1164.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: We strongly support permitting publicly owned pools to nonprofit partners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: It would be game-changing for water safety and aquatics access and equity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: But the bill asks New York City Parks to evaluate and coordinate across multiple agencies, a responsibility that goes beyond Parks'core expertise and mission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: That is a natural function for a dedicated coordinating body like the Office of Water Safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: On extending the beach and pool season, Intro 262, we strongly support giving New Yorkers more time in the water.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: But our longer season is not possible without long-needed reforms to the lifeguard corps to support realistic staffing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: We recommend an intensive review and evaluation of current lifeguard training and retention in order to build a more positive lifeguard culture and sustainable workforce.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: And on water safety signage, Intro 957 and 1163, we strongly support multilingual water safety signs at all beach entrances and high visibility areas like lifeguard chairs and jetties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: This is an achievable, sensible way to improve and promote water safety with prime examples of this strategy across the United States.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: We recommend four things in closing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: First,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Introduce the Office of Water Safety legislation alongside today's bills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Second, hold a follow-up hearing in January 2027 with adequate notice for nonprofits, community groups, parents, and victims'families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Third, pair any season extension with lifeguard core reforms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: And fourth, consider a water safety education in schools bill as part of a unified package.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Together, these measures could form a robust policy package for the new year, one that addresses systemic barriers to coordination, expands how water safety and learn to swim is taught and shared,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: builds capacity across agencies and nonprofits, and lays the groundwork for a citywide water safety action plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: The coalition stands ready to work with this committee, the council, and the administration to make it a reality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify on this important issue and your commitment to continued collaboration on how New York City can strengthen its citywide approach to water safety.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Sean, pardon my slow writing.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Can you go back to the third request?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shanna Blanchard
utterances.text: Pair any season extension with lifeguard core reforms.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Testify.

chapters.summary: Bridget Klopinski, president of the Rockaway Beach Civic Association, says the community supports extending evening hours but wants lifeguards in chairs, not just nearby. She warns an 8 a.m. opening conflicts with surfing and fishing, says fall extension enters hurricane and nor'easter season, asks for coverage on Senior Skip Day, tailored beach policies, and fewer intermittent closures.
chapters.title: Bridget Klopinski describes Rockaway beach season and ocean safety concerns

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You're mine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Now it's on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Hi, Chair Hankerson and committee and advocates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: I didn't prepare remarks because I only learned about the hearing last night, but it felt important to be here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: I know we share concerns about water safety, expanding access, and all of these topics.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: My name is Bridget Klopinski.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: I'm a resident of the Rockaways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: And currently serving as the president of the Rockaway Beach Civic Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Our organization is also a member of the Water Safety Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: So I'm just here to share some firsthand experience as a resident of the Rockaways and someone who loves the ocean, and I'm in the ocean as much as I possibly can be, and if I'm not in it, I'm near it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: So about intro 0262, about hours, and also the length of the beach season.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Specifically speaking to Rockaway, there seems to be longstanding and widespread consensus on extending the hours into the evening, perhaps 7 or 8 p.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: That's long been a community conversation and request, even necessitating split shifts or other mechanisms to make that happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: So expanded hours seems to be a common request in the evening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: If hours are extended or lifeguards are kept nearby,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: as they are currently in heat waves, it would be an ask of mine that they be kept in the chairs or on the sand, not just in the shacks, because we know in the event of a rescue, seconds count.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: So while we acknowledge that lifeguards are being kept in the facilities longer during heat wave events,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Could we consider having them in the chairs?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: As far as the earlier morning proposed, the 8 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: For an ocean-facing beach community like Rockaway, that feels early.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: There are a lot of other ocean recreation activities that are hugely popular, such as surfing, fishing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: The optimal hours are 6 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: To 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Those activities are not permitted on beaches when lifeguards are posted during the lifeguard hours and locations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: So my question would be what accommodations would be made for those other activities in an ocean-facing community like Rockaway?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Wow, I have a lot to get through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Length of the season, I just want to acknowledge that extending into the fall is extending into hurricane season and nor'easters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: We've already experienced strong nor'easters this year and did as early as September.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: So the ocean temperatures are colder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: The conditions are more volatile.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: That can't be disregarded in an ocean community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Perhaps decoupling the conversation from pools and beaches and even beaches that don't have wave activity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: It's an important consideration because the conditions in Rockaway are unique and present unique challenges to our lifeguard force.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Just to a point of Council Member Narcissus' question about the outside of hours or outside of seasons,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: fatalities or drownings that we've had, I just want to signal to the Council, Senior Skip Day is something that happens every May right before Memorial Day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: We often have a loss of life immediately before the official beach opening season.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Please look at that day in particular, even if the lifeguard season is not expanded, to have additional personnel on the beaches, whether that's PEP or lifeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: It could literally save lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: To Councilmember Murano's point, just about tailoring to each beach, that seems to make a lot of sense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: I know it's not easy to do in a broad agency perspective, but the conditions at Coney Island or Orchard Beach are not the same as they are in Rockaway Beach, and that absolutely has to be acknowledged, which I guess just goes into my last point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: We need to develop a culture of ocean literacy and ocean competence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: There's been a lot of conversation today about when the lifeguards are on the chairs and when they're not and what those different statistics mean.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: In recent years, there have been more and more days and occasions that lifeguards are taken off the chairs on a sunny day because the waves are head high, as good as Rockaway gets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Waves are a feature of ocean recreation, and we need to, as rescue personnel and also...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Beach visitors and local resident swimmers, we need to have access to those conditions as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: to develop stamina, understanding, respect for the conditions, but to just close the beach or pull guards off chairs every time there's a three or four foot wave, even within the summer season,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: is not fostering that aquatic culture that we need to save lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: And I think before we talk about expanding access in terms of season, I would like to see less intermittent closures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: And I'm curious, I would like to ask the council to follow up about statistics on how many hours within the beach season and regular lifeguard hours this summer,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: the guards were off the chairs either because of a rip current advisory, a shark sighting, or any of these other factors that are deeply impacting the hours that like the guards should be on the chairs, but perhaps are not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: I can think of, and I would be happy to share dates and occasions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: I don't know if it's a rip current advisory going out from OEM or a weather bulletin that sort of signals that, but to pull guards off the chairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: During rip current events as opposed to enhancing the staffing during those events is a huge disservice to the public.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bridget Klopinski
utterances.text: I'll close.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you for your insight and perspective.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Carl Quigley, a lifetime aquatic professional, says the Council should consult water safety experts. He stresses access to pools for nonprofits and lifeguard training, asks about AED locations and daily water checks, criticizes uneven lifeguard deployment in the Rockaways, and says pools should be permitted like other sports facilities.
chapters.title: Carl Quigley calls for pool permitting and aquatic culture investment

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Councilman Hankerson and all the council members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: And I want to thank my colleagues behind me that testified.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: And I'd like to just echo ditto to almost everything that they said.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: They're spot on in almost every element of this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: I just want to, by the way, I'm Carl Quigley.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: I am a lifetime aquatic professional.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: I'm a former.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: A college swim coach, high school swim coach, water polo coach, rockaway lifeguard, teacher of swimming, coached people from and taught people from infancy up to Olympics.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: So there's a, and the people in the audience that testified have a vast

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: background of knowledge, it would behoove the people that are making decisions to reach out to this group, the Water Safety

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Council, the coalition, that they're willing to work and give their insights in terms of going forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: I'm just going to address number one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: As someone who ran, and I was an assistant athletic director at St.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Francis College, getting access to swimming pools is essential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: When I worked there, we had a potpourri.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: of different entities that used our pool.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: And we manned the city beaches with people who used our little 25 by six lane pool,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: whether they were high school swimming teams or such, college athletes and such.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: People who went through our lifeguard program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: But as a lifeguard instructor after I retired, I could not find a place that would rent a space to me to maintain my certification.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Either I had to piggyback with another organization or something.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: So it's a significant issue, and that's the issue of aquatic culture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Aquatic culture is making, not just having a swim, open swim at a public pool for an hour or two a week.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: It's a consistency because to get the 35 seconds and then to swim the distance swim, you need to be a pretty proficient swimmer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: And you want the lifeguard that's on the chair to be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Feel competent that they can do the job, not that they're just there, and that if someone is floundering in the pool or the ocean, that they can get them, retrieve them, and bring them to safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Just a couple other things that I'm sorry I went over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: AEDs on the beach, I'm not sure how many they are, so I'd like you guys to see if you can find out where they are, where they're located.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Who has them and who's trained to give AED help to your victims?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: Rip currents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: I think lifeguards should also be as part of training every morning, having been a rough, grockery resident, to just be on the beach and go into your chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: You should go in the water and check the actual space that you're guarding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: And finally, the deployment of lifeguards, how they're deployed across the length of the beach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: It's something that should be looked at.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: In the Rockaways, you'll have a clump of lifeguards in the 140s, and then nobody in the 130s, and then a couple more in the 120s, and then there's vast deserts where there are no lifeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: This summer in the Rockaways, coming up,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: 116th Street will be open for the first time since

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: As long as I can remember, a lot of the areas are going to be opened back up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: And the whole idea of aquatic culture and not to go at Gateway National Park, a neighbor of Rockaway, they only opened eight beaches, eight towers last summer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: The culture that they can

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: upon to demand their beaches is not there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: So the idea of opening New York City Department of Parks pools to people who have expertise in swimming, in water polo, in lifeguarding, in learn to swim is essential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: I can't, if there's anything that this meeting comes out, that has to happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: We permit hockey rinks, we permit tennis courts, we permit soccer fields, we permit baseball fields.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: What about a swimming pool?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: The Catholic Youth Organization puts so many lifeguards on the beaches in Rockaway and in Brooklyn and Coney Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: It's essential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carl Quigley
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olga Perez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Vicki Hsu, development director at Friends of Plus Pool, says a longer season requires lifeguard reforms. She notes Plus Pool certified 61 of 64 participants in three weekends and asks to shorten certification to align with YMCA and Red Cross and make it year-round; she supports signage but says school education reaches all children and asks for more advance notice of hearings.
chapters.title: Vicki Hsu urges shorter year-round lifeguard certification and school water safety

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Hankerson and members of the committee that was here and also everyone that's here to listen to the testimonies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: My name is Vicki Hsu and I am the Development Director at Friends of Plus Pool.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Thank you for holding the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Friends of Plus Pool is a nonprofit working to bring free, accessible swimming to New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: To date, we have provided free, life-saving water safety instruction to over 2,300 low-income children and adults.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: We are proud members of the Water Safety Coalition and support...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Everyone's testimony that's testified today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: But we want to talk about two of the recommendations our coalition has introduced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: The first one is around the longer season.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: A longer season requires stronger lifeguards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: We strongly support extending the beach and pool season, but especially as summers get hotter, New Yorkers need more time in safe water, especially those with few pools and little shoreline access.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: But more days on the calendar mean nothing if there are not enough lifeguards to staff them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: As the coalition said, a longer season depends on reforms that support realistic staffing in a sustainable lifeguard career pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: We need to shorten the New York City lifeguard certification program so it aligns with those of the YMCA and the American Red Cross and make it year-round so it's not just once a year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: In 2024, Plus Pool, in partnership with the Henry Street Settlement and the Splash Fit Swim Club,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: certified 20 lifeguards every weekend for three weeks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Actually, over 20 people every three weeks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Of the 64 enrolled, 61 became certified lifeguards and were on to get jobs in different pools throughout the city, representing a 98% pass rate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: So we know it's possible to train lifeguards, especially to work in the pools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Water safety must start in the classroom, and this is regarding the signage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Signage is important, and we support Intro 957 and T20262714.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: But signs reach people only when they're already at the water, and also, even if they're at the water, they're probably not paying attention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: I don't pay attention to any signs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Maybe because I'm a swimmer, but I just don't pay attention to them that much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: While Local 6 legislation to require the Parks and Recreation Department to develop water safety materials and provide them to the Department of Education for distribution is in effect, we have yet to see any resources materialize.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Given the infrastructural and economic challenges to teach all children how to swim, teaching water safety in school is the most equitable way to reach every child, regardless of income or neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Today's hearing is just a start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: We respectfully ask that in the future, critical stakeholders in such important and life-saving legislation are alerted to the hearing a little bit more in advance,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: allowing us sufficient time to review proposed bills, reflect, and comment on them with our experience and expertise that will ensure

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: that the bills are as impactful as possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: We, the people in this room testifying today, have hands-on experience working to address water safety and have a lot to contribute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: We cannot fully endorse any bill currently as written, but we look forward to continuing collaboration with the committee, the city council, and the administration to address the systemic barriers to comprehensive citywide water safety action plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vicki Hsu
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Hankerson notes there are no online participants or additional sign-ups. He apologizes for late notice, commits to a follow-up hearing and meeting with the coalition, jokes that someone must teach him to swim, and adjourns the November 13 Parks hearing on water safety.

summary: Committee on Parks and Recreation held a hearing on water safety at city beaches and pools, considering Intros 262, 957, 1163, and 1164.

Parks Department testified that the 2026 season was the longest in a decade with 1,174 lifeguards, 16.7 million visitors, and zero on-duty drownings, but raised operational and budget concerns with season/hours and signage bills.

Public witnesses from water safety nonprofits and community groups urged an Office of Water Safety, school-based water safety education, expanded pool access, lifeguard corps reforms, and more advance notice for hearings.
